the Higgs branching ratio can be determined to within 5% for a Higgs mass between 120 and 160 GeV/c2 with a 500 GeV/c2 Linear Collider, using an inner radius of 1.2cm, a hit precision of 3 μm, and a luminosity of 1033 cm-2 s-1.

the Higgs branching ratio can be determined with a precision of 0.5% at the 1 TeV Linear Collider with a CCD vertex detector, that a small beampipe radius (1.2 cm) and high hit precision (3 μm) are preferred, that a beampipe radius of 2.4cm and a hit precision of 5 μm are also acceptable, but that a larger radius and a lower hit precision will degrade the measurement precision.

the optimization of the vertex detector for Higgs branching ratios at the Linear Collider.
the design of a vertex detector for the Linear Collider.
the design of a vertex detector for a future Linear Collider experiment.

the vertex detector design for the Linear Collider is well understood and optimized.
the vertex detector is not a limiting factor to Higgs branching ratio precision measurements at a 500 GeV Linear Collider.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Higgs branching ratio precision is not sensitive to the inner vertex detector radius, and that it is sensitive to the vertex detector hit precision.
the Higgs branching ratio can be measured with an accuracy of better than 10% at a Linear Collider with a CCD vertex detector.
a 1% uncertainty is achievable for a 100 fb-1 data sample, and a 2% uncertainty for a 10 fb-1 sample, with a 5 μm hit resolution, and 1.2-2.4 cm beampipe radius.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a CCD vertex detector with a 2.4-cm beampipe radius and 5-μm hit precision is capable of measuring the Higgs branching ratio to within 5% of the expected values for the SM-like Higgs boson mass of 125 GeV, and the 1.5-TeV CM energy.
the CCD vertex detector is an excellent choice for the next generation vertex detector at a Linear Collider.
